_link.title: I can identify which aspects of collision theory are affected by a change in concentration

toLevel2.stem: Which aspect of collision theory is affected by increasing the concentration of a reactant?
distractors: Collision energy
Particle orientation
Activation energy

toLevel2.stem: Increasing the concentration of a reactant does NOT affect:
distractors: The frequency of collisions
The number of collisions per second
How often particles meet each other

toLevel2.stem: What happens to the number of collisions per second when concentration is increased?
distractors: It decreases
It stays the same
It first increases then decreases

toLevel2.stem: Does changing concentration affect the orientation of particle collisions?
distractors: Yes, it improves orientation
Yes, it worsens orientation
Yes, it eliminates the need for correct orientation

toLevel2.stem: Which of the following is increased when concentration is raised?
distractors: The kinetic energy of each particle
The activation energy of the reaction
The proportion of correctly oriented collisions

toLevel2.stem: Increasing concentration increases the frequency of collisions between reactant particles.
distractors: False

toLevel2.stem: Increasing concentration increases the kinetic energy of individual particles.
distractors: True

toLevel2.stem: Increasing concentration increases collision {{blank:1}} but does not affect the {{blank:2}} of individual collisions.
distractors: energy
frequency
orientation
speed

toLevel2.stem: When concentration is increased, there are more {{blank:1}} in a given volume, leading to more {{blank:2}} per second.
distractors: products
reactions
catalysts
orientations

toLevel2.stem: Changing concentration affects collision {{blank:1}} only and has no effect on collision {{blank:2}} or activation energy.
distractors: energy
frequency
orientation
rate

toLevel3.stem: Why does increasing concentration increase the frequency of collisions?
toLevel3.answer: More particles per unit volume means they encounter each other more often
distractors: The particles move faster when there are more of them present
The activation energy decreases when more particles are added
The particles align in better orientations at higher concentration

toLevel3.stem: Why doesn't increasing concentration change the kinetic energy of individual particles?
toLevel3.answer: Kinetic energy depends on temperature, not on the number of particles
distractors: Adding more particles absorbs energy from the existing particles
Concentration and kinetic energy are measured in the same units
Kinetic energy is only affected by the presence of a catalyst

toLevel3.stem: A student doubles the concentration of NaOH in a reaction. What is the effect on collision theory factors?
toLevel3.answer: Collision frequency increases but energy and orientation per collision are unchanged
distractors: Both collision frequency and energy per collision increase equally
Collision energy increases but frequency stays the same as before
Orientation improves because particles are closer together in solution

toLevel3.stem: How does increased collision frequency lead to a faster reaction rate?
toLevel3.answer: More collisions per second means more chances for successful collisions
distractors: More collisions per second means each collision has more energy
More collisions per second lowers the activation energy barrier
More collisions per second improves the orientation of particles

toLevel3.stem: Why is it important to distinguish between collision frequency and collision energy when explaining concentration effects?
toLevel3.answer: Precise identification of the affected factor gives accurate exam answers
distractors: Both factors are always affected equally by any change in conditions
Collision energy is the only factor that matters for reaction rate
Collision frequency has no impact on reaction rate at all

toLevel3.stem: If concentration is halved, what happens to the proportion of particles with energy exceeding Ea?
toLevel3.answer: It remains the same — energy distribution is unchanged
distractors: It halves because fewer particles are available to react
It doubles because each remaining particle has more energy
It drops to zero because the reaction can no longer proceed

toLevel3.stem: Increasing concentration increases the rate because there are more collisions per second, giving more opportunities for successful reactions.
distractors: False

toLevel3.stem: Kinetic energy of particles depends on {{blank:1}}, not on {{blank:2}}, so concentration changes do not alter particle energy.
distractors: concentration
temperature
pressure
volume

toLevel3.stem: More particles per unit volume means particles {{blank:1}} each other more often, increasing collision {{blank:2}}.
distractors: avoid
energy
repel
orientation

toLevel3.stem: Even though concentration does not change the energy per collision, the overall rate increases because there are more {{blank:1}} for {{blank:2}} collisions to occur.
distractors: barriers
energetic
catalysts
oriented

toLevel4.stem: A student adds more hydrochloric acid to a reaction with magnesium ribbon. Using collision theory, which factor explains the increased rate?
toLevel4.answer: More HCl particles per unit volume increases collision frequency
distractors: The HCl particles now have higher kinetic energy per particle
The activation energy of the reaction has been reduced
The magnesium particles now collide in better orientations

toLevel4.stem: A chemist dilutes a reactant solution to half its original concentration. Which collision theory factor is affected and how?
toLevel4.answer: Collision frequency decreases because there are fewer particles per volume
distractors: Collision energy decreases because particles are further apart
Orientation improves because particles have more space to align
Activation energy increases because the solution is more dilute

toLevel4.stem: In an industrial process, the concentration of a reactant is tripled. A student writes: 'This increases the energy of each collision.' Is this correct?
toLevel4.answer: No — only collision frequency increases, not energy per collision
distractors: Yes — more concentrated solutions always have more energetic particles
Yes — tripling concentration triples the energy of each collision
No — concentration changes do not affect any aspect of collision theory

toLevel4.stem: A student investigates the effect of concentration on the rate of reaction between sodium thiosulfate and hydrochloric acid. They increase [Na₂S₂O₃]. Which collision theory aspect changes?
distractors: Particle orientation improves
Activation energy decreases
Kinetic energy per particle increases

toLevel4.stem: Two beakers contain the same reaction. Beaker A has a concentration of 0.5 M and Beaker B has 1.0 M. Both are at the same temperature. How do the collision theory factors compare?
toLevel4.answer: Beaker B has higher collision frequency but the same energy per collision
distractors: Beaker B has higher collision energy but the same collision frequency
Beaker A has higher collision frequency due to more space for particles
Both beakers have identical collision frequency and energy per collision

toLevel4.stem: A student states: 'Increasing concentration is like increasing temperature because both speed up reactions.' Why is this comparison incomplete?
toLevel4.answer: Concentration affects frequency only, while temperature also affects collision energy
distractors: Concentration and temperature affect exactly the same collision theory factors
Temperature affects frequency only, while concentration also affects energy
Neither concentration nor temperature affects any collision theory factor

toLevel4.stem: An enzyme-catalysed reaction slows down as the substrate concentration drops. Using collision theory, which factor explains this slowdown?
toLevel4.answer: Fewer substrate particles results in fewer collisions with enzyme molecules
distractors: The enzyme particles lose kinetic energy as substrate is consumed
The activation energy increases as substrate concentration drops
The orientation of enzyme-substrate collisions becomes less favourable

toLevel4.stem: When a student increases the concentration of HCl in a reaction with Mg, the collision {{blank:1}} increases but the {{blank:2}} energy per collision stays the same.
distractors: energy
potential
orientation
activation

toLevel4.stem: Diluting a solution reduces the number of {{blank:1}} per unit volume, which decreases collision {{blank:2}}.
distractors: products
energy
catalysts
orientation

toLevel4.stem: Unlike temperature, changing concentration does not affect the {{blank:1}} of individual particles, so it only changes the {{blank:2}} of collisions.
distractors: mass
orientation
size
direction

toLevel5.stem: A student claims that doubling concentration doubles the rate of reaction. Under what condition would this claim be most accurate?
toLevel5.answer: When the rate depends directly on the concentration of that reactant
distractors: When the temperature is also doubled at the same time
When the reaction has zero activation energy barrier
When the reaction is occurring in an open system only

toLevel5.stem: A student increases both concentration and temperature simultaneously. How should they separate the effects when analysing the results?
toLevel5.answer: Concentration affects only frequency; temperature affects both frequency and energy
distractors: Both factors affect only collision frequency in exactly the same way
Both factors affect only collision energy in exactly the same way
The effects cannot be separated because they are always identical

toLevel5.stem: A peer writes: 'Increasing concentration increases rate because particles collide harder.' Evaluate this explanation.
toLevel5.answer: Incorrect — concentration increases how often particles collide, not how hard
distractors: Correct — more particles in a space means each collision is more forceful
Incorrect — concentration has no effect on reaction rate at all
Correct — harder collisions mean more energy is available per collision

toLevel5.stem: Compare the effects of increasing concentration and adding a catalyst on collision theory. Which statement is correct?
toLevel5.answer: Concentration increases frequency; a catalyst provides a lower Ea pathway
distractors: Both increase collision frequency by the same mechanism
Both lower the activation energy of the reaction equally
Concentration lowers Ea while a catalyst increases frequency

toLevel5.stem: A student argues: 'Since concentration doesn't change collision energy, it can't significantly affect reaction rate.' Is this reasoning valid?
toLevel5.answer: No — increased frequency alone provides many more opportunities for successful collisions
distractors: Yes — collision energy is the only factor that determines reaction rate
Yes — frequency has no measurable effect on the rate of a reaction
No — concentration actually does increase collision energy significantly

toLevel5.stem: In a Maxwell-Boltzmann diagram, how would increasing concentration change the curve?
toLevel5.answer: The curve shape stays the same because the energy distribution is unchanged
distractors: The curve shifts to the right because particles have more energy
The curve becomes broader because there are more particles present
The curve peak increases because more particles have the modal energy

toLevel5.stem: A student says: 'Concentration and surface area both increase rate by the same mechanism.' Evaluate this claim.
toLevel5.answer: Correct — both increase collision frequency without changing energy or orientation
distractors: Incorrect — concentration increases energy while surface area increases frequency
Incorrect — surface area lowers Ea while concentration increases frequency
Correct — both lower the activation energy of the reaction equally

toLevel5.stem: A reaction reaches completion faster at higher concentration. A student attributes this entirely to 'more energetic collisions.' What is the flaw in this reasoning?
toLevel5.answer: The energy per collision is unchanged; the faster rate is due to more frequent collisions
distractors: There is no flaw — higher concentration always increases collision energy
The flaw is that completion time is unrelated to concentration changes
The flaw is that energetic collisions only occur at higher temperatures

toLevel5.stem: Concentration and surface area both increase reaction rate by increasing collision {{blank:1}}, while temperature also increases collision {{blank:2}}.
distractors: energy
frequency
orientation
mass

toLevel5.stem: Saying concentration makes particles 'collide harder' is {{blank:1}} because concentration changes how {{blank:2}} particles collide, not how energetically.
distractors: correct
slowly
accurate
rarely
